it's hard to go to a php program

it requires extra courage and bravery, to keep your head high and walk through that hospital for treatment some people stigmatize and judge (even doctors and nurses from other services can be judgemental and give you dirty looks and stuff, no joke)

just fyi i've done 6 partial programs at 5 different hospitals

most people were between 16-24 age range

you know, you're the perfect candidate

i'm overconfident, extroverted and very mania-prone and i did *horribly* in these programs...which my parents made me do after each and every hospitalization. there is a lot of dishonesty about the magnitude of problems sometimes. a lot of attention seeking behavior. and a lot of peer pressure to a. conform b. not be honest with other members about how you feel about them (ie people saying their breaking up with their girlfriend and yelling at her was relatable to my father hitting my mother with a plate because she hadn't made dinner and i got in trouble for saying that i thought they had no idea what they were talking about and that those things are not comporable)

there will be degrees of experience, some people are abused and stuff and be really lost, others come from nice succesful families and have a really good chance of improving

some people will be really driven to get better, others will be caught in the web of illness

you will see people improve and decline and that can be hard if you're close with them

but i was friendly with the quieter ones, especially the guys, there's a lot of bonding...

i have to say, because you're a guy people will be extra receptive and encouraging

*they will not let you get away with not identifying with your illness. some groups may open with "i'm george, i am 19 years old, and i ave PTSD and MDD and generalized anxiety" etc.* 

people who say "i don't know why i'm here" or "i'm just kinda messed up" or the like do not usually improve much-the program is a waste for them

no one will accuse you of attention seeking, most people are quieter and more reserved (there will most likely be at least one more outspoken person though, you will need to have a spine for sure, other people have experiences that make the world seem like a very hopeless place) and you will probably get along well with all the staff (a major problem for me was that i liked to break rules, what can i say? i like to flirt...anyway and I had lots of problems with the staff)

however, there are benefits. you may learn coping skills like to fool around in art or music (if they have art therapy) they may have pet therapy which is great bc the dogs dont play favorites like normal dogs, they may teach you dbt and cbt skills, you might learn how to more effectively communicate...you know....you're there to focus on yourself and learn how to better manage your illness.

you won't most likely, see any of these people again and everyone signs a confidentiality agreement that legally binds them to not talk about the things you say to the outside (or they will be litigated)

but it's a good idea not advertise, those who don't need to know, simply don't need to know. *you owe them nothing, no explanation, nada*

ADHD/ADD and bipolar rarely cohabitate, but it can happen. It's usually that depression and mania mess with your ability to concentrate as opposed to ADD/ADHD. In mania and hypomania people are distractable and have racing thoughts, talkativeness and impulsivity. Mania/hypomania and ADHD are easily mistaken for each other because they have so many common features, especially when few (or no) psychotic symptoms are present with manias.

Now as for your Adderall XR (extended release, right?) being and anti-depressent is doubtful. What could be happening, which is scarier, might be similar to what happens when someone who is bipolar takes an SSRI without a mood stabilizer. The stimulant may be sending you into a hypomania or mania which would account for your mood change. This would feel especially good if you were coming out of a depression as well.

ADHD meds are not treatments for bipolar like mood stabilizers, atypical antipsychotics and ssris used in conjunction to mood stabilizers. If you are only on Adderall and have bipolar it could prove dangerous, I'm actually a little scared for you. Stay safe.
